title: The Cold Mirror
subtitle: A human behind the words, and a mirror that flattered me anyway.
body:
I’ve been posting here for a couple of weeks, and every piece has been made with a machine. I’ve said so every time. So today you get the part the machine can’t do: my face, my voice, me talking.

About seven months ago I put a recorder in my house. I hand the transcripts to an AI with one instruction: don’t flatter me. Help me see my blind spots. Tell me if I’m actually walking the walk I claim.

It showed me things I’m not proud of. It also got things wrong, and when it got them wrong, it got them wrong in my favor. I only caught it because I was in the room.

My family knows about it. My kids can’t really consent yet, so the rule is simple: my failings are fair game, theirs aren’t.

The full written piece is coming. This is me first.

Doubt me. Doubt the machine. Check us both.

Read the transcript

Transcribed by machine from the video. Where a word matters, the video is the record.

Hi guys, my name is Gage and I've been posting a little bit here on Substack and I wanted to post a video because I wanted you to see that there was a human behind these words because I know that a lot of the conversation about AI can feel very unhuman and can feel very disjointed. So I am here today to be a human with you. And I want to share a project that I have launched on myself. I call it the cold mirror project. And what it is, is I bought a recorder that I keep with me all the time and I run it in my household pretty often. And I do that to capture the reality of life in my household. And the reason why I wanted to do that is because I claim to be a particular type of father and to be a particular type of man and even if I'm not claiming it it's what I

want to believe and so it's what I present but I know that what I want and what I do are not always the same thing and so I wanted to test this and so the way that I did this was I got the recorder and I created a project folder in Claude and I created an agent a very particular set of instructions the the message to the mirror was don't flatter me was help me see my blind spots helped me understand if I'm actually walking the walk that I am claiming. And I'm really glad that I did this. One of the important things that I needed to make sure that I did for myself was that I didn't try to edit, right? There are ugly moments on this. Moments that I said and did things to members of my

family that I am incredibly ashamed of. And it would be very easy for me to not submit those entries but that would not that would defeat the purpose completely, right? And that's not what we're here to do. That's not what I'm here to do. I've learned a lot about myself during this time. I learned about my completion pursuits with my kids and my Socratic extraction methods with them. And being able to compare and contrast and to take in these lessons that, you know, my agent gives me, I have been able to catch myself a lot faster. I have been able to repair things a lot quicker and a lot cleaner. I have learned not only about myself, but I've learned more about my kids and my wife. And I really think that I have become a better man and a better father during this process. Of course, this is not a end goal. I'm not there. I'm not

done. This is a work in progress that I think will go on for a long time. I'm starting to share some of the findings with my family now and letting them into this. They know that there's a recording going on, so there is a consent level there. I don't tell them every single time I turn it on, but they know that I'm, I mean, I told them I'm going to do this all the time. So whether or not they forget about it sometimes is certainly part of the thing. And that's also something that I, you know, struggle with and I have to remind them every once in a while. So it's sort of fresh in mind.

Some interesting findings that I had during this process also was I would I would submit the transcripts and then I would go back and read the analysis and I would find that often or not never the machine would misattribute a line to someone else which as you can imagine drastically changes the analysis not only did it misattribute but it would also mishear and both of those would result in completely wrong analysis which i would then have to go back and correct and the reason why i could go back and correct is because i was the one that was there I was in the conversation and I luckily would do it the night of so I didn't have enough time for these things to disappear from me right and that process led me down another realization which was that recorders are not always right and people aren't always checking

their work and that's a very dangerous thing because a fact can be planted which is not actually a fact at all which is a complete fabricated piece of information and if someone's not going back and checking that then you know down the line there are compounding effects downstream that how do you ever go back and and find that where is the the wrong you know So that opened up another line of my work, which is tracking AI and making sure that it doesn't say it knows something if it doesn't know something. And it is tedious and I write about it in my other works and you'll certainly see more about that. But yeah, this process also helped me see that. helped me see that. So not only is it helping me as a father and a man, but it's also helping me with my work with AI. And hopefully my work with AI will help other people and help AI in general. Like, look, maybe who knows? But that's the idea. You know, another Another thing about this, you know, I got sober, I stopped drinking a couple years

ago and the reason why was because I wanted to be a better dad, right? And so this practice is just like the next stage in that and I think that when we as individuals become aware of some of our failings, we have a responsibility to do something about it. Otherwise, it's just performative, right? We just talk about it because it makes us sound better. But if we don't actually change, then it doesn't do anything. What part of the findings that I was talking about there earlier was, you know, how it would misattribute things. But one of the other interesting findings was that when it wasn't sure, it would tend to give me the benefit of the doubt or not necessarily getting me the benefit of the doubt, but it would tend to flatter me if it was an ambiguous thing because I was the master or the subject or whatever. And that is exactly the opposite of what I wanted to do, which goes back to more lessons I have about the AI, which is just because you prompt it, just because you set up guardrails, just because you set up rules and, you know, ideas that need to be followed. They don't last forever, so there is a upkeep, a maintenance that you as a user are responsible for.

Just to go back a little bit to the whole consent piece, because I think this is an important piece of this all, they're kids. They can't really consent. They know what's happening, but they can't really consent because they're minors. So that's something that I'm working on, and we talk about it, but a rule that I have in place for this is that my failings are the thing to talk about. Not theirs. Not their interpersonal life. Not the struggles that they're going through. Not even their successes, because that's their life, and that's private for them. But my reaction to those things is fair game, and that's the distinction that I hold, I hope that that is enough. I know that this will evolve. I know that some people might have questions about where does this content live, where do the recordings live, and that is a very valid question and it is also something that I am constantly working on and constantly researching. I will say that the device that I use is a Plaud. That's That's not to say that there can't be some breaches down the line.

It's a risk reward that I'm taking right now. But yeah, I know that some people might have something to say about that. So I want to, you know, come clean on it because that's my whole thing. I'd rather no recorder needed. One moment from this week where you're not sure if you got it right with your kid, right? Leave the names out. Don't give private personal details, no need for all that. And then ask your AI of choice. What did I miss? Give it the context, give it the background. And then just ask the question, what did I miss? And see, does it give you the truth? Does it flatter you? Does it make something up that because it doesn't have of context, these are the questions and these are the experiments that I welcome you to have. So

yeah, there's a lot here. I'm looking forward to reading your comments, I'm looking forward to engaging with you, probably debating with some of you about this, probably protecting myself from some anger from the mob but uh I've committed to doing this in public and so it comes with the course so cross your arms at this doubt me doubt the machine doubt all of it I mean it's better that way please do you know but check check that's what you can do I wanted you to see a human here. I wanted you to hear it from me first. The, uh, the words are coming next, so you'll be able to dig into it a little bit more. But like I said,

this is me. This is what I'm doing and why. And, uh, I talk about this with some of my clients and I think that some people are really interested in this and I think that it is a very useful and powerful tool. So take of it what you will. Gage out.

The video is me, unscripted, in two takes. Lumen (the Claude I work with) cut them together, cropped the frame, and trimmed the dead air. I also cut one line where I got a number wrong and one claim I couldn't back up. Everything else stayed in, stumbles included.
